## Theoretical and empirical estimands {#what-is-your-estimand}

```{r}
#| label: lundberg-pipeline
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3
# Lundberg et al. (2021) three steps as boxes-and-arrows (ggplot, editable).
steps <- tibble::tibble(
  x = c(1, 2, 3),
  lab = c("Theoretical\nestimand",
          "Empirical\nestimand",
          "Estimation\nstrategy"),
  sub = c("unit quantity +\ntarget population",
          "identification\nassumptions (DAG)",
          "where the R\ncode enters")
)
ggplot2::ggplot(steps, ggplot2::aes(x, 1)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(width = 0.8, height = 0.7, fill = ncl_blue) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = lab), colour = "white", fontface = "bold",
            size = 5.2, vjust = -0.3) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sub), colour = "white", size = 3.6, vjust = 2.0) +
  ggplot2::annotate("segment", x = 1.42, xend = 1.58, y = 1, yend = 1,
           arrow = ggplot2::arrow(length = ggplot2::unit(0.18, "cm")), linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::annotate("segment", x = 2.42, xend = 2.58, y = 1, yend = 1,
           arrow = ggplot2::arrow(length = ggplot2::unit(0.18, "cm")), linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 3.5)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_void()
```

::: {.none}
- The theoretical estimand is stated **outside** any model – before R opens
:::

::: {.src}
@LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand.
:::

::: notes
Our five analysts and the twenty-nine teams of the red-card study were all given a question in words, and none of them was told exactly which quantity would answer it. Lundberg and colleagues call that quantity the estimand, and the title of their paper asks for it: "What is your estimand?" They split the answer into three steps. The theoretical estimand is a quantity defined for each unit, together with a target population, stated in words before any model exists. The empirical estimand is what corresponds to that quantity in the data that can be observed, and making that link brings the assumptions of identification into the open, which is the job of the causal graph. Only the third step, estimation, involves R. When the authors reviewed the thirty-two quantitative articles of the 2018 volume of the American Sociological Review, they could state the quantity for each unit with confidence in only five.
:::
